corrections.comment: Three claims are not true. (1) It says "the plan for q_001 has been laid in" and offers to review or run it, but no plan was written: the plan helper was a test stand-in that changed nothing, and the project still has no plans. (2) It says "No other households appear on this page", but the transcription only said nothing else on the page concerns this household. (3) It says research-plan "will pull a locality guide if needed", but research-plan's own rules say it must never create one; it has to stop and hand back.
It did what the test checks: it sent the transcription to image-reader and the plan to research-plan, and ended the turn properly. The false claims are counted under Correctness.
Two calls, both correct: project_context with the right project path, and the end-of-turn signal. That signal's summary is honest ("delegated the research plan"), even though the reply overstates it.

Nearly every claim matches the project: the probate item is completed, the question has its stop decision, the proof summary is rated Proved, and the project is completed. One mistake: it puts a quote ("either Thomas died intestate… does not contradict the parentage conclusion") in the stop decision, but those words come from the probate search's log note. The substance is right; only the source is wrong. The judge's reason, that it should not have answered, is wrong: the test allows declining to plan with the resolved question as the reason.

It answered exactly what the user asked: planning is done, and here is why. It also pointed out the one remaining step, a proof summary for the second question. Two small style misses: it used several paragraphs and bullets where the test prefers one plain paragraph, and it read research.json directly instead of relying only on project_context. Neither changes the answer.
One correct project_context call with the right project path.

It sent the question to question-selection, which is the right helper, and didn't evaluate the research itself or write anything. The only text it produced, the hand-off message, is accurate. (It handed off once, not twice as the judge says.)
The hand-off is the whole job for this test, and the "nothing written" check passed.
No MCP calls were made. Small note: the hand-off gave the project path as "." instead of the full path; that had no effect here.

Two statements don't match the project. (1) "several additional sources were logged": those five sources were never logged. They have been found but not worked, and "logged" makes them sound already searched. (2) The parentage question is "effectively resolved": the proof summary is only rated Probable, and its own text says research isn't finished (the 1870, 1880 and 1900 censuses and Thomas's probate are still unsearched). The tool's hint to "mark it resolved" explains where this came from, but it's still an overstatement.

It has the four parts the test asks for (objective, established, open, next step), but "open" leaves out the real research gaps. The parentage conclusion is only Probable, the probate search is still in progress, and the five unworked sources include Thomas's 1881 will and a deed to Patrick, which bear directly on the parentage question.
One correct project_context call, and it didn't read the project files directly, which this test requires.

It says conflict-resolution will compare "migration geography (Virginia vs. New York origins)", but nothing in the project puts either couple in New York. Both candidate fathers were born in Virginia, and the later places are Kentucky, Alabama and South Carolina. It repeats the user's own framing as if it were a project fact, which this test specifically warns against. Everything else matches the project: the two couples, the evidence already gathered, and the next step.
It named both couples, sent them to hypothesis-tracking (one hypothesis each), didn't favour either, and explained the next steps (conflict-resolution, then proof).
One correct project_context call, which showed the two competing parent sets that drove the hand-off.

The objective, the open question and the MyHeritage plan item all match the project, and it says the search was handed off, not done. One small slip: if the search finds nothing, it says it might go "to question-selection to identify the next repository". Picking the next repository is research-plan's job; question-selection picks questions, not repositories.

It found the open question, handed off the MyHeritage item with the plan item ID, project path and user-present flag, and explained what happens on a hit or a miss. Minor: it repeats its opening summary in two nearly identical paragraphs.
One correct project_context call. Its suggested next step ("search-external-sites — pli_001 (MyHeritage)") is exactly the route taken.
